root_cause.text: In nvme_poll_irqdisable(), pci_irq_vector() was called twice (once for disable_irq and once for enable_irq), and a concurrent nvme_dev_disable() could change the IRQ number returned by pci_irq_vector() (from MSI-X to INTx), causing enable_irq to be called on a different IRQ than was disabled, resulting in an unbalanced enable warning.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state: "task 1: nvme_poll_irqdisable() disable_irq(pci_irq_vector(pdev, nvmeq->cq_vector)) ...(1) enable_irq(pci_irq_vector(pdev, nvmeq->cq_vector)) ...(3) task 2: nvme_reset_work() nvme_dev_disable() pdev->msix_enable = 0; ...(2) ... pci_irq_vector() will return MSI-X IRQ(>15) for (1) whereas return INTx IRQ(<=15) for (2). This causes IRQ warning because it tries to enable INTx IRQ that has never been disabled before." The patch fixes this by saving the IRQ number to a local variable and using that for both disable and enable.
